chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The woman whose husband dies while he is absent, her waiting period (iddah) begins from the day the news reaches her, whether the testimony is established or not.
ai.seo_question: When does a wife's waiting period begin if her husband dies while he is away?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the commencement of the iddah for a widow whose husband dies in his absence. The ruling establishes that the waiting period begins upon the receipt of news, irrespective of whether the testimony is deemed legally conclusive or not, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical certainty in marital status changes. This principle ensures clarity in lineage and remarriage eligibility during periods of uncertainty regarding the spouse's fate.
